title: IMGT reference V and J amino-acid sequences, IMGT-gapped
source: IMGT/GENE-DB via GENElect query 7.3 (V-REGION and J-REGION, amino acid, IMGT gaps preserved), https://www.imgt.org/genedb/, Homo sapiens
licence: CC BY 4.0. www.imgt.org terms of use, section 'Conditions of use and license': "The IMGT(R) data are provided to both public and private users under the CC BY-4.0 license." Verified by reading that page on the retrieval date.
citation: IMGT(R), the international ImMunoGeneTics information system(R), Lefranc M-P et al. IMGT unique numbering for immunoglobulin and T cell receptor variable domains and Ig superfamily V-like domains, Dev Comp Immunol 27:55-77 (2003), PMID 12477501.
notes: A V entry's `gapped` string is the IMGT-gapped amino-acid V-REGION: index i (1-based) IS IMGT position i, and '.' is an IMGT gap slot rather than a residue. Every functional non-partial entry below carries Cys at index 104, which is the 2nd-CYS anchor - that is what makes position transfer from this profile exact rather than inferred.

TRBV and TRBJ are present so a T-cell receptor beta chain is IDENTIFIED and REJECTED, not numbered as an immunoglobulin. TRAV/TRAJ could not be retrieved (IMGT rate-limited the request), so a TCR alpha chain is caught only by the germline bit-score floor, not by name.
Only functional (F) non-partial alleles are included; ORF and pseudogene alleles are not a numbering reference.
